method: Independent direct HTTP status, final-URL, media-type, byte-length and SHA-256 checks; page-level visual review of image-based company and Alaska airport PDFs; parsed page-level review of the FAA decision; and a current ownership, financing, construction, opening and exit sweep through the research cutoff

verifiedClaims: Tiger currently publishes NorthLink Aviation as a North American Transportation portfolio company
The live page attributes NorthLink to Fund III, gives a 2021 initial-investment year and describes the 55-year, 120-acre airport project
The manager page supports continuing Tiger sponsorship but does not disclose the control percentage or current minority cap table
Tiger announced on November 3, 2021 that it acquired a controlling interest in IC Alaska Airport LLC and renamed the company NorthLink Aviation
NorthLink simultaneously executed a 55-year lease with the State of Alaska for the 120-acre South Park campus
Investment Company of Alaska, a C Change Group subsidiary, was identified as the original project sponsor
The release distinguishes company equity from the State airport lease and does not disclose Tiger's exact percentage or acquisition vehicle
Tiger's April 2022 Fund III closing release identifies the vehicle as a growth-infrastructure fund
The release supports the fund and infrastructure-strategy basis used with Tiger's NorthLink portfolio attribution
NorthLink's May 2022 public presentation calls Tiger Infrastructure the owner and controlling investor
The same presentation calls Alaska Future Fund an owner and co-investor
The presentation establishes historical co-ownership but does not publish percentages or prove Alaska Future Fund's status at the August 2026 cutoff
FAA identifies the privately funded project at the South Airpark lot leased to NorthLink under ADA-32351 and quotes the authorized cargo-facility use
The approved design includes an 80-acre apron, 15 hardstands, a 90,000-square-foot warehouse and related fueling, glycol and ground-service infrastructure
FAA approval concerns the airport-layout amendment and development of the leasehold; it is not evidence of State ownership in NorthLink equity
AIAS reports that NorthLink broke ground in 2023 but performed only limited construction in 2024
Main construction had not begun when the Q1-Q2 2025 report was written, and the first phased hardstand development was then targeted for summer 2026
AIAS identifies Cathay Pacific as an anchor tenant and reports annual lease revenue of $924,736
AIAS's latest reviewed annual report calls NorthLink an ongoing cargo development with phased construction
The report states that six hardstands are planned by 2027
The latest official status supports an active development-stage project but not a completed or operating terminal
NorthLink announced Alaska Future Fund's investment on November 30, 2021
The release identifies Barings as manager of the Alaska Future Fund and the fund as part of Alaska Permanent Fund Corporation's Alaska Investment Program
The release does not disclose percentage ownership or a later current-status statement

exitSearch.result: No public NorthLink equity raise, construction financing, ownership transfer, asset sale, signed pending transaction, terminal opening or Tiger exit was identified by the cutoff. Tiger's live Fund III portfolio page and the airport's current phased-construction reporting support continuing Tiger control and an active project; Alaska Future Fund's and C Change's exact current equity status remain unresolved.

responseSourceHealthCorrections: Alaska Future Fund is directly supported as a November 2021 investor and a May 2022 owner/co-investor, but no later primary source proves that it remains a current owner; its current status must remain unresolved.
Investment Company of Alaska was the original sponsor, but the reviewed sources do not disclose whether it or C Change retained equity after Tiger acquired control.
ADA-32351 is a State airport lease/concession and must not be represented as State of Alaska equity in NorthLink.
The current buildout is an active, delayed and phased development; neither the 2023 groundbreaking nor the customer agreements establish terminal opening or operating cargo throughput.

The latest reviewed scale is 15 planned stands and a 90,000-square-foot warehouse, with six hardstands planned by 2027; the repository's roughly 100,000-square-foot initial-terminal wording is not retained as a completed operating fact.
